scope: Current checked-out source code; schedules are configured behavior, not proof of live job success. The separate flora-extractor repository was not inspected.

nodes.title: Extractor CSV: candidate study pairs
nodes.summary: The separate flora-extractor project supplies extracted replication/original pairs. This app downloads its CSV and turns eligible pairs into records people can review.
inputs: flora-extractor/data/extracted.csv from the configured GitHub repository and branch.
The extractor's data/retired_pairs.csv, pinned to the same source commit, supplies explicit retirement requests.
steps: Resolve a source commit, download its CSV, save a timestamped archive, and validate the candidate against the previous snapshot.
Import resolved, valid pairs into PostgreSQL. A new pair receives a record, extraction metadata, and human_1, human_2 and llm queue slots.
Existing pairs refresh extractor-owned values while retaining human decisions; an unambiguous source-slot match can preserve identity when the pair key changes.
Promote the imported bytes to extracted_latest.csv and verify their checksum.
saves: PostgreSQL: unvalidated, record_metadata and validation_queue.
Server working files: data/extracted_latest.csv and timestamped archives, or EXTRACTOR_DATA_DIR when configured.
Durable imported snapshots: extractor_snapshots; run status, safety report and logs: extractor_maintenance_runs.
refresh: The app schedules the full maintenance pipeline at 02:00 UTC daily.
An administrator can queue a run from the Extractor pipeline panel; the server checks that queue every 10 seconds.
New imported pairs are eligible for the next queue request after the import transaction commits.
outputs: Reviewable candidate pairs and an audited, imported extractor snapshot.
cautions: Paper discovery, screening and original-study matching happen upstream; those scripts are outside this checkout.
An imported candidate is not yet an approved record or a prepared FLoRA output.
Local CSV archives are working files; the PostgreSQL snapshot copy is the durable application record.

nodes.title: Extractor maintenance: sync, report, retire
nodes.summary: This pipeline refreshes the human-review input and reports or retires obsolete extractor pairs. It is separate from the pipeline that builds the final FLoRA dataset.
inputs: A scheduled or admin-queued maintenance run.
A verified extractor snapshot and, for retirement, its matching retired_pairs.csv manifest.
steps: Take a PostgreSQL advisory lock so one executor owns maintenance.
Run sync_csv.py to download, validate, import and verify promotion.
For a full run, backfill OpenAlex work IDs after a successful sync; an enrichment failure is a warning.
Run find_orphans.py against the verified snapshot to describe missing pairs without deleting them.
When automatic retirement is enabled, archive and retire only eligible, untouched pairs explicitly listed in the source manifest.
saves: extractor_maintenance_runs stores queued/running/final status, per-stage results, logs and safety evidence.
retired_records stores the complete archived record before eligible review records and their dependent data are removed.
A combined server log defaults to logs/extractor_maintenance.log.
refresh: Nightly at 02:00 UTC, or when an admin-queued run is picked up by the 10-second dispatcher.
Each stage updates the run history; dependent stages are skipped when prerequisites fail.
outputs: An updated validation queue, a read-only orphan summary, and an explicit retirement report.
cautions: Missing from the latest CSV does not mean delete: many missing pairs are intentionally withheld validated work.
Retirement is disabled by EXTRACTOR_AUTO_RETIRE=0/off and is capped by EXTRACTOR_MAX_RETIRE_PERCENT (default 15%). Human-worked records are protected.
This pipeline does not build output/flora.csv.

nodes.title: Published entry sheets
nodes.summary: Published Google Sheets are another input route. Their accepted rows are copied into the Source Records collection, alongside the app's approved records.
inputs: Enabled source definitions in sources.yml: Replications, Reproductions, FReD Replication Success and SCORE 2025 Validation in this checkout.
Per-source column mappings, UUID column, validation column and accepted status values.
steps: Fetch each enabled sheet as CSV; check CSV format, headers and row-count floor before accepting it.
Skip an unchanged payload by checksum. Filter to accepted validation values, or accept all rows for a source explicitly configured without a validation column.
Validate promoted values before writing. Skip missing/invalid UUIDs and all rows sharing a duplicated sheet UUID.
Insert only new (source, sheet_row_id) identities. Commit each source independently and record its result.
saves: source_records stores imported fields, the original raw row, source identity and a friendly display ID.
source_sync_runs stores per-source timestamps, counts, failures and payload SHA-256.
snapshots/<source>.csv stores the fetched payload on that executor; the nightly workflow uploads these as 90-day artifacts.
refresh: Source Records → Run pipeline runs this stage on demand.
GitHub Actions runs Sync entry sheets at 03:00 UTC daily; it can also be started manually.
New rows appear after source commit and a new grid request.
outputs: A combined Source Records input collection with provenance and sync history.
cautions: Sheet sync is insert-only: changing an already-imported UUID's sheet cells does not overwrite the existing database record.
Corrections are made on the derived FLoRA record; this importer does not write changes back to Google Sheets.
The backup FReD source is disabled in sources.yml.

nodes.title: Approved records join Source Records
nodes.summary: sync_validated.py copies the application's approved records into the same input collection as the entry sheets, so one final preparation can combine both routes.
inputs: Rows in the validated table after human/admin publication decisions.
steps: Shape each validated record into Source Records columns and preserve the approved row's identity as its sheet_row_id.
Insert missing records; update changed, unreviewed rows while retaining their display IDs.
Protect legacy rows already marked as human-reviewed.
Mark source rows deleted when their original validated row no longer exists; keep their identities and provenance.
saves: source_records under the app-validation source, plus source_sync_runs counters.
refresh: Runs during Source Records → Run pipeline and the nightly 03:00 UTC Sync entry sheets workflow.
Approving a validation record does not itself run this bridge or build the final FLoRA CSV.
outputs: The app's approved data is available to the combined FLoRA transform.
cautions: This is different from export_validated.py, which writes a separate validated-only CSV.
A protected reviewed row may differ from its current validated origin and needs human investigation.

nodes.title: Exclusions, outcomes and paper metadata
nodes.summary: Supporting inputs tell preparation which rows to exclude, how outcome wording maps to the codebook, and which bibliographic details belong to each paper.
inputs: The exclusions sheet and checked-in notebook/COS exclusion lists.
outcome_alias, administrator duplicate/preprint rulings and FLoRA corrections.
OpenAlex metadata for DOIs and work IDs, with reference-based fallbacks.
steps: sync_exclusions.py replaces only its own source groups in transform_exclusions; manually added exclusions stay intact.
enrich_works.py fetches uncached paper metadata and stores found and missing results.
The transform reads these inputs to normalize outcomes, choose correct identifiers, enrich references and apply deliberate exclusions.
saves: transform_exclusions, work_metadata, outcome_alias and preprint_dedup_decisions in PostgreSQL.
FLoRA corrections are stored separately in flora_record_changes.
refresh: Exclusions and metadata enrichment are stages of the website and nightly FLoRA pipelines.
Metadata is cached; normal enrichment is mainly for uncached records, with explicit retry options for misses.
outputs: Rules and cached evidence used by the prepared dataset.
cautions: A pair-specific exclusion can exclude one original/replication relationship without excluding every use of the replication paper.
Changing a rule can change the derived FLoRA view before a new full stored snapshot is prepared.

nodes.title: Run pipeline: the background job
nodes.summary: The Source Records Run pipeline button queues a durable job. A server worker then refreshes inputs, builds the combined FLoRA data, checks it, and stores the result.
inputs: An authenticated admin request to POST /api/admin/source-sync/dispatch.
Current sheets, approved records, exclusions, metadata and saved FLoRA decisions.
steps: Save a queued source_sync_jobs row and return its job ID immediately.
The 5-second dispatcher takes an advisory lock and marks one queued job running.
Run entry sheets → exclusions → validated records → DOI metadata → FLoRA IDs as separate subprocess stages.
If all those stages pass, run prepare_flora.py in a fresh per-run output directory with a 15-minute network-check budget.
Store the run's CSV and reports in the database, copy conventional artifacts to server output/, and finish the job.
saves: source_sync_jobs: requester, status, timestamps, log_text, artifact_csv, report_json, report_markdown and optional recovery_csv.
The stages update their respective input tables; preparation updates flora_data.
Server output/ receives a local copy of completed artifacts.
refresh: Queue pickup is normally within the next 5-second tick when a worker is available; total runtime can be minutes.
The UI polls the job, so queued/running and final result are separate states.
Download links are bound to that run's durable artifact rather than whichever file currently happens to be on one server.
outputs: A combined stored dataset plus an exact run CSV, JSON report and Markdown report.
cautions: Source refresh stages run independently, but any failure prevents the final preparation stage.
A successful run with warnings can say needs review; that is different from a failed run.
The website does not commit GitHub or upload to OSF. Use the separate Publish FLoRA workflow for the repository copy.

nodes.title: Clean, combine and deduplicate
nodes.summary: The transform converts raw source rows into a consistent FLoRA record: clean identifiers, standard outcomes, joined paper metadata, deliberate duplicate choices and traceable provenance.
inputs: Active source_records plus outcome aliases, exclusions, cached metadata, duplicate decisions and saved corrections.
steps: Normalize replication outcomes and derive reproduction outcomes from the independent computation and robustness axes.
Clean DOI/URL/text values and expand recognized COS quote shorthand.
Apply confirmed preprint/publication decisions, pair-aware exclusions, duplicate rules and metadata/reference fallbacks.
Retain the source record and merged-source provenance for each resulting record.
Attach permanent IDs and saved FLoRA corrections before export; log and omit export rows missing either title.
saves: build() is read-only and returns a prepared DataFrame.
run() pins identities through flora_registry, then writes the requested candidate CSV and diagnostic CSVs.
refresh: The FLoRA admin view rebuilds from current inputs when its cache signature changes.
The final stored CSV/API snapshot changes when preparation stores the dataset, or an eligible existing FLoRA record is corrected directly.
outputs: A prepared dataset with consistent fields, source provenance and stable identities.
Diagnostics for missing titles, merged outcome conflicts, preprint candidates and cross-type duplicate rulings.
cautions: The FLoRA tab is a current derived view; it can include an untitled record that the exported dataset omits.
Unknown outcome aliases or invalid axes block export rather than silently becoming blank.
Simply viewing the derived table is not the same as storing a new complete snapshot.

nodes.title: Permanent FLoRA IDs
nodes.summary: The identity registry connects combined records to permanent published IDs so a title or DOI correction does not renumber the dataset.
inputs: The transformed records and their source/merged-source identities.
Existing flora_records registry and the supplied reference export identity/order.
steps: Match existing source provenance to existing registry records.
Allocate IDs and publication positions for new records.
Keep earlier publication positions reserved and append new records.
Export id and its full lowercase MD5 as id_md5; the digest is based on the permanent ID, not on a title.
saves: flora_records keeps permanent registry identities and positions.
flora_dataset_history keeps dataset count history.
flora_data carries the resulting id, id_md5 and export_position.
refresh: The FLoRA IDs stage runs after source sync and enrichment.
Standalone preparation also registers the exact transformed frame before exporting it.
outputs: Stable row identifiers, stable lookup hashes and a predictable output order.
cautions: IDs are not regenerated from changing paper titles or DOIs.
Retiring a stored row preserves its identity; the same ID can be reactivated later.

nodes.title: Prepare and check the exact CSV
nodes.summary: prepare_flora.py builds one candidate CSV, checks those exact bytes, stores its data, and writes the release files. This is the final stage shared by the website and nightly pipeline.
inputs: The combined transform, current permanent identities and saved FLoRA corrections.
Structural rules and network evidence/cache.
steps: Capture the stored dataset revision, build a fresh .flora.candidate.csv, and verify nonblank unique IDs plus correct MD5 hashes.
Run structural checks and network checks on that candidate; report findings, skipped targets and deferred targets.
Create a release manifest, notes and daily count history for the candidate bytes.
Commit the snapshot to flora_data, preserving concurrently corrected rows and rejecting an older build when another complete snapshot won the race.
Replace local output files, with flora.csv last; write the final preparation report.
saves: flora_data and flora_data_metadata for the stored dataset.
output/flora.csv, flora_release_manifest.json, flora_release_notes.md, flora_history.csv and flora_dataset_summary.md.
Preparation/structural/network reports and diagnostic CSVs in the selected output directory.
refresh: Runs after successful input stages of a website or nightly pipeline.
Stored data becomes available when the database commit succeeds; local file replacement is a subsequent step.
outputs: The combined CSV and matching validation/release evidence.
cautions: Check findings normally produce needs_attention warnings; identity errors, transform errors and other exceptions fail the run.
A late file-write failure can occur after the database committed. The report then identifies a recovery CSV; do not assume failed means the stored dataset is unchanged.
This command does not publish to GitHub or OSF. --input is offline/non-storing by default unless --store-data is explicit.

nodes.title: Stored dataset: flora_data
nodes.summary: flora_data is the durable prepared FLoRA snapshot used by Download full CSV and the public API. It is different from raw source records and human-review records.
inputs: A complete prepared snapshot, or a direct correction to an already-stored active FLoRA record.
steps: Insert new IDs and update changed data without changing identities or positions.
Mark IDs absent from a new snapshot retired instead of deleting them.
Reactivate returning IDs with their original positions.
Update shared revision metadata so readers know the dataset changed.
saves: PostgreSQL flora_data: prepared values, permanent identity, extra fields, position, version and retirement timestamp.
PostgreSQL flora_data_metadata: output columns, snapshot fingerprint and update time.
refresh: After a successful prepare/store transaction.
After Save on an eligible active record already present in flora_data; records not yet stored require a pipeline run.
outputs: Current complete CSV export and active records for public lookup endpoints.
cautions: PostgreSQL is the durable store. A server's output/flora.csv is a separate filesystem copy.
Concurrent corrections are preserved during a long build, so an immutable build artifact can differ from the latest stored export.
No empty full snapshot is accepted by default.

nodes.title: Save a FLoRA correction
nodes.summary: Save records a correction with its author and history, then updates the prepared view. If that record already has an eligible active stored row, it also updates the data served by the API and full CSV immediately.
inputs: Edited fields, optional per-field notes and the version of the FLoRA record opened in the editor.
steps: Validate field values and refuse a stale editor version if another person saved first.
Append the effective corrections and change history under the permanent FLoRA identity.
Rebuild the record's derived values, including consequences such as metadata for a corrected DOI.
Write changed fields to its active flora_data row and move the public dataset revision when eligible.
saves: flora_record_changes is the append-only correction history.
flora_data and flora_data_metadata update for eligible already-stored records.
Raw imported sheet cells and upstream extractor output remain their original inputs.
refresh: The corrected record appears in the next current FLoRA view request.
Eligible stored corrections are visible to a fresh API server request after commit, subject to downstream HTTP caches.
Repository output/flora.csv updates only after a nightly build or the Publish FLoRA Action.
outputs: An auditable correction that persists through future builds, and an updated stored record where applicable.
cautions: Save does not write back to Google Sheets or commit GitHub.
If the row is not stored yet, is retired, or becomes untitled, direct stored publication does not happen; run the pipeline to reconcile the whole snapshot.
Restore is another logged change; history is not erased.

nodes.title: Automatic checks after updates
nodes.summary: Background entry checks inspect the stored dataset and keep findings for the FLoRA tab. They report possible problems; they do not correct records.
inputs: The stored flora_data CSV, current revision, and shared network-check cache.
steps: Every five minutes, ask whether structural or network checks are due.
Run structural checks when the stored dataset revision has changed.
Run network checks once per UTC day from 04:00, with a 45-minute budget.
Store findings by record and check key. Resolve findings when the relevant check no longer finds the issue; retain a person's dismissals.
saves: flora_check_runs and flora_check_findings.
Network successes/DOI lookups use link_checks and original_doi_lookups.
refresh: A correction can wait for the next five-minute structural-check tick before its finding changes.
Network checks are daily from 04:00 UTC; a time budget can defer targets.
A failed structural run has a one-hour retry delay.
outputs: Per-record findings and run summaries in the FLoRA admin interface.
cautions: Checking does not modify FLoRA values.
Not a problem records a human dismissal; it does not change the dataset value or delete the audit evidence.
A cached successful link check is intentionally reused for roughly 25–35 days.

nodes.title: Three different CSV downloads
nodes.summary: A run CSV, the current full FLoRA CSV and a filtered table export answer different questions. Their bytes can differ after corrections or later runs.
inputs: The chosen export route: a pipeline run, current stored data, or the current admin filters.
steps: Run CSV: read that job's immutable artifact_csv from source_sync_jobs.
Download full CSV: export the current active flora_data rows in publication order.
Filtered FLoRA export: export the current derived FLoRA view matching its filters.
Source Records export: download raw source collection rows matching its filters.
saves: A downloaded copy on the user's computer; reading an export does not rebuild the pipeline.
Run snapshots remain in source_sync_jobs independently of later stored changes.
refresh: Run artifacts remain fixed to the completed run.
Current full export reflects stored corrections and completed snapshot commits.
Filtered exports reflect their selected collection and active filters when requested.
outputs: CSV files appropriate for run audit, current publication data or filtered investigation.
cautions: Compare like with like: a run CSV is evidence of that run, while the current full export can include later changes.
A filtered derived view can include rows omitted from the title-required final export.

nodes.title: Public FLoRA API
nodes.summary: Public clients search and look up the stored FLoRA dataset. Requests read PostgreSQL through a read-only transaction and never start an import or preparation run.
inputs: Requests to /v1/prefix-lookup, /v1/original-lookup, /v1/dois, /v1/search and /v1/id-lookup.
The active stored flora_data dataset.
steps: Validate query values and limits.
Read the shared dataset revision; reuse an in-process projection only when its database/revision key still matches.
Return DOI-level records, title/search matches or permanent ID-hash records as requested.
saves: No dataset writes. A process-local projection cache improves read performance.
refresh: A request reaching the server checks the database revision each time.
HTTP responses allow a 300-second cache for search and 3600 seconds for other successful endpoints; a browser/proxy may show older data until its cache expires.
outputs: JSON lookup/search results for public consumers.
cautions: The API reads the stored snapshot, not the raw source_records table or the local output/flora.csv file.
If no dataset has been stored yet, the API reports dataset not ready (503).
id-lookup expects the entire 32-character ID MD5; DOI-prefix lookup uses three hexadecimal characters of the DOI hash.

nodes.title: Publish the repository copy
nodes.summary: The Publish FLoRA GitHub Action writes the currently stored dataset to output/flora.csv and commits the release files so other repositories can read them.
inputs: The current active flora_data snapshot, including eligible corrections saved since the last build.
Optionally, a successful website pipeline job ID whose report should accompany the same bytes.
steps: Read the stored dataset and revision together in a read-only repeatable-read transaction.
Write flora.csv, a matching manifest and release notes, and daily count history.
Include a website run's reports only if its CSV fingerprint matches these current bytes; remove stale build-specific reports otherwise.
Commit and push the configured release files when flora.csv changed.
saves: GitHub repository: output/flora.csv and the files listed in .github/release-files.txt.
The script itself writes files; the GitHub workflow performs the commit/push.
refresh: Automatically after Sync entry sheets completes, whether that sync succeeded or failed.
Manually through Actions → Publish FLoRA, for example after a website Run pipeline or a saved correction.
The successful nightly Sync entry sheets workflow also commits its freshly built release.
outputs: A versioned repository release copy for downstream readers.
cautions: A website button run and Save do not themselves trigger a GitHub commit.
After a failed nightly build, this workflow can still publish the last stored dataset with saved corrections; it does not retry source preparation.
No OSF upload is performed by these workflows.

nodes.title: Separate validated-only export
nodes.summary: A different daily workflow exports only the application's approved validation records. It is not the combined FLoRA release containing entry sheets.
inputs: validated rows and bibliographic reference lookups/cache.
steps: Read approved records and prepare citation/reference fields.
Write the validated-only CSV and a list of references needing manual attention.
Commit changed export files and the reference cache back to the repository.
saves: data/validated_export.csv, data/needs_manual_refs.csv and oa_ref_cache.json.
refresh: GitHub Actions Daily validated export is scheduled for 04:00 UTC daily and supports manual dispatch.
outputs: Approved app records as a separate CSV and a manual-reference follow-up file.
cautions: This does not build the combined output/flora.csv or store flora_data.
GitHub schedules are configured start times, not a guarantee of exact completion or success.

nodes.title: When updates happen
nodes.summary: Saving, refreshing sources, preparing a snapshot, checking it and committing GitHub are separate events. All configured daily schedules use UTC.
inputs: Admin actions, the app's running scheduler and enabled GitHub Actions workflows.
steps: 00:22 UTC: retry eligible failed Gemini tiebreakers in the app.
02:00 UTC: run extractor maintenance in the app.
03:00 UTC: GitHub Sync entry sheets refreshes sources, prepares/stores the combined FLoRA dataset and commits a successful release.
After that workflow completes: Publish FLoRA exports the current stored data, including corrections, to the repository.
04:00 UTC: GitHub Daily validated export runs; the app's network entry checks also become due for the day.

Continuously: dispatch source jobs every 5 seconds, extractor jobs every 10 seconds, check entry-check due status every 5 minutes, reap stale validator slots every 2 minutes and run housekeeping hourly.
saves: Each job saves to its own run/audit tables and/or output files as described on its detail card.
refresh: For Berlin on 29 October 2026 (CET), add one hour to UTC: 02:00 → 03:00, 03:00 → 04:00, 04:00 → 05:00. During CEST add two hours.
Manual buttons can run the relevant job earlier; browser refresh only reloads data and does not run a pipeline.
A queue polling interval is not a promised completion time.
outputs: A predictable update sequence with separate evidence for each successful or failed stage.
cautions: These are schedules found in code, not a live verification that deployment workers or GitHub jobs are currently healthy.
The app scheduler must be running for in-process jobs; external network and job runtime can delay completion.
Public HTTP caches can delay a visible API update even after a successful database save.
